title: Chromosome 7 — anatomy and region assembly
clinical_history: Use this demonstration ideogram to learn p/q orientation and reconstruct chromosome 7 at region-level resolution. Numbering begins at the centromere and increases toward each telomere.
hints: The short arm (p) is at the top, ending at pter. The long arm (q) is below the centromere.
On each arm, band numbers increase as you move away from the centromere toward the telomere.
At this resolution, 7p2 is the distal short arm and 7p1 is the proximal short arm.
explanation: A standard human chromosome is drawn pter → p arm → centromere → q arm → qter. Region-level labels such as 7p2 and 7q3 name the chromosome, the arm, and the region. Finer bands (7q22) and sub-bands (7q22.1) nest inside that hierarchy.
plain_language_interpretation: A normal chromosome 7 reconstructed from major p-arm regions, the centromere, and major q-arm regions.
